newsitem.title: GERMANY: Coffee roaster KJS says price rise not ruled out.
newsitem.headline: Coffee roaster KJS says price rise not ruled out.

text.p: German coffee roaster Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), part of Philip Morris, said on Friday it could not rule out further retail price increases in its roasted coffee products if futures rises were maintained.
It said the February 8 announcement that prices would rise by two marks per kilo effective March 10 no longer looked sufficient.
Prices may have to be raised by yet another two marks.
German coffee roasters Alois Dallmayr Kaffee oHG and J.J. Darboven said they would probably match any additional price rise by KJS.
Most roasters, including Dallmayr and Darboven, last Friday said they would implement increases of two marks.
"There is no question that this level already is not sufficient to meet rising costs," said Dallmayr manager and co-owner Wolfgang Wille.
An official at Darboven said he envisaged an increase of four marks if KJS increased prices by that amount on March 10.
Eduscho GmbH & Co KG and Melitta Kaffee GmbH could not be immediately contacted.
A spokesman for Tchibo-Frisch-Roest-Kaffee GmbH said the company, which plans a price increases of one mark per kilo on February 27, had no immediate plans to add to this.
Tchibo has its stores, while the other roasters operate through wholesale and retail chains.
